Hypothesis: When a user makes a high value product search without appending terms like "review" they are likely to be ready to purchase.
Hypothesis: For high cost items, customer reviews are necessary but not sufficient to make users comfortable with a purchase
Hypothesis: CTAs will be low for FS interventions on high cost products when prefixes like "best" or "top" are appended to the product category in search query.
Hypothesis: Even for low cost items, users want to do some cursory browsing for pricing and aesthetics.
This fakespot intervention to improve opt-in needs to be non-invasive so as to let the user complete their primary task without engaging with this opt-in
Hypothesis: When a user appends Amazon to a search, they would rather go directly to a relevant product page than leverage a quick action to search with Amazon.
Hypothesis: CTRs on general low cost item searches ("eraser") will be relatively high
Hypothesis: We will see a higher CTA when a user makes a category search for a low cost item ("best eraser") vs a high cost item ("best tv")
